subject: Aurora: throughput surge, 503s — mitigation, ownership and closure plan
messages:
From: Santiago Alvarez <santiago@auroraretail.com>
To: jonas_weber, marissa_cole, kimberly_park
Cc: eng+aurora@auroraretail.com
Date: 2027-03-29T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Immediate: Significant throughput spike and 503s affecting checkout - Aurora

Team —

We started seeing a sudden throughput spike around 08:45 PDT that correlates with 5xx responses on several checkout routes. Traffic itself did not look anomalous on our side (no new campaigns), so this looks like a serving-side regression. Impact: ~15% of checkout requests returned 503 in the earlier 20m window; conversion drop was visible on our dashboards.

We're opening this to Redwood as an urgent incident — the spike hit a major holiday uplift and we need a mitigation plan immediately. Can you confirm:
- What immediate mitigations you can push (routing, model fallback, or cache priming)?
- ETA for next status update?

I've attached the KPI snapshot and the exact time slices we saw (aurora_throughput_kpis.csv).

Thanks —
Santiago
Director, Infrastructure
Aurora Retail

[attachment: aurora_throughput_kpis.csv]

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Santiago Alvarez <santiago@auroraretail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole, kimberly_park, aditya_rao, david_kim
Date: 2027-03-29T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Immediate: Significant throughput spike and 503s affecting checkout - Aurora

Santiago — thanks for the alert and the data. We're on it. Quick triage notes and immediate plan:

1) Mitigation (now):
- Turn on fast-fallback routing to the lower-LAT CPU-backed variant we keep for hotfailures (will reduce throughput capacity but eliminates the 503s). ETA: 4 minutes to stage; 10 minutes to full rollout.
- Enable prefix caching for 15 minutes on the busiest checkout prefixes to reduce token-invocation pressure.

2) Short-term stabilizers (30–90m):
- Temporarily reduce batch sizes for the most latency-sensitive routes to avoid queue saturation.
- Add temporary rate limit back-pressure on non-critical analytics requests from the Aurora integration.

3) Investigation steps (in parallel):
- Capture model-serving node logs and kernel metrics.
- Reproduce the spike against a preserved copy of yesterday's traffic slice.

I'll lead the incident bridge and share the bridge link in 2 minutes. Marissa — can you coordinate commercial outreach (credits/exec note) if this is classified as an SLA-impacting event? Kimberly/David/Aditya — will take ownership of triage, kernel trace, and routing tweaks respectively.

Jonas Weber
Head of Runtime Ops
Redwood Inference

[attachment: initial_triage_notes.txt]

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Santiago Alvarez <santiago@auroraretail.com>, Claire Huang <claire.ops@auroraretail.com>
Cc: jonas_weber, kimberly_park, aditya_rao, david_kim
Date: 2027-03-29T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Immediate: Significant throughput spike and 503s affecting checkout - Aurora

Santiago / Claire —

First, sorry for the disruption. We're executing the mitigations Jonas outlined — you should see error rates drop within the next 15 minutes. From a customer-facing standpoint, next steps and commitments:

- Short window mitigation: Jonas and the runtime team will run fast-fallback routing and prefix caching. Target: < 15 minutes to visible reduction; we will confirm 30m trending after mitigations.
- Full RCA & fix: We will deliver a root-cause analysis and a permanent remedial plan within 7 business days.
- Customer protection: we'll apply a one-time usage credit proportional to impacted tokens and work with you on an SLA remediation credit if the final RCA confirms service-side degradation.

Internal owners: I will coordinate the executive notification and a consolidated post-incident packet. Kimberly — please draft the customer-facing postmortem language and a proposed credit calculation by EOD. Aditya — please pull capacity planning numbers and whether reserved pools were hit.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Claire Huang <claire.ops@auroraretail.com>
To: marissa_cole, jonas_weber
Cc: Santiago Alvarez <santiago@auroraretail.com>, eng+aurora@auroraretail.com
Date: 2027-03-29T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Immediate: Significant throughput spike and 503s affecting checkout - Aurora

Thanks — we see error rates moving down to baseline (~1% from 15%) after the routing change. Appreciate the quick action. Two asks while you investigate:

1) Can you confirm whether this was triggered by a serving-side kernel regression (we saw kernel-level timeouts in our traces) versus an unexpected workload pattern we should throttle?
2) We will need a timeline for the permanent fix and an estimate for any credit. Can you provide early numbers so our finance/comms teams can prepare?

Claire
SRE Lead, Aurora Retail

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole, jonas_weber, aditya_rao, david_kim
Cc: Santiago Alvarez <santiago@auroraretail.com>, Claire Huang <claire.ops@auroraretail.com>
Date: 2027-04-06T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Closure: Aurora throughput anomaly — RCA summary, owners, and action tracker

Team — following the triage and weekend analysis, here is the consolidated closure and action tracker (attached: stability-playbook-draft.pdf). Summary:

Root cause (condensed):
- A regression in a recently landed GPU kernel selector caused suboptimal kernel pairing for certain sequence-length distributions; this led to queue buildup and timeouts on ~12% of requests under Aurora's checkout workload profile.
- The regression was introduced by an automatic kernel ranking change in release 2027.3.12 that failed to account for variable batch tail latencies.

Immediate corrective actions taken:
- Fast-fallback routing to CPU-backed variant (rolled back after stabilization) — prevented further 503s.
- Reduced batch sizes for checkout routes during peak windows; adjusted autoscaler ramp rates.

Owners & timeline (high level):
- Runtime kernel fix: aditya_rao — patch and validation in staging by 2027-04-08, rollout window 2027-04-11.
- Permanent routing guardrails (avoid automatic kernel rank flips under hot load): david_kim — policy change by 2027-04-09.
- Customer-facing artifacts: marissa_cole — post-incident note + credit proposal by 2027-04-07.
- Stability playbook update: kimberly_park — playbook v0.2 published (attached) and internal runbook for manual fallback.

Customer remediation:
- Proposed credit: 12% of the monthly minimum committed token spend for March 2027, pending final sign-off from Finance (account: Aurora Retail). Marissa — please confirm if this aligns with earlier guidance.

Next steps:
- We will schedule a 30-minute readout with Aurora execs the week of 2027-04-12 to walk through RCA and the preventive roadmap.
- Weekly follow-through: owner updates in the SUP-4482 ticket; I'll consolidate progress every Monday.

Thanks everyone for the quick collaboration — closing the incident channel but leaving the RCA ticket open until actions are verified.

Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
